clue.text: Doctor swears this animal caught rodent, one with fur, near hospital

parts.note: the hippo is a large African animal
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
a rat is a rodent
the Roman numeral I is one
an animal's coat is its fur
H is the abbreviation for hospital, as on road signs

explanation.surface: A gruesome menagerie of hippo, rat and furry creature turns up beside a hospital, making a doctor curse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swears' looks like cursing, but the definition means the pledge a doctor takes; 'with' and 'near' simply join the pieces in order.
explanation.definitionFit: The ancient medical pledge attributed to Hippocrates is traditionally sworn by new doctors.

clue.text: Rider appearing gaunt

explanation.surface: A horseman looks worn out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rider' is a forename: H. Rider Haggard wrote King Solomon's Mines.
explanation.definitionFit: H. Rider Haggard is the Victorian novelist; haggard also means looking exhausted and drawn.

clue.text: Exponent of physical force

explanation.surface: Someone who champions brute strength.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Exponent' looks like a champion of something; here it is the mathematical index, as in two to the power three.
explanation.definitionFit: In maths an exponent is also called a power; physical strength or energy is likewise power.

clue.text: Other people interrupting continually, but improving

indicators.note: one piece breaking into the middle of another, so it is placed inside

parts.note: on end means continually, as in talking for hours on end
them means other people, as in us and them

explanation.surface: A patient keeps getting interrupted by visitors but is getting better anyway.
explanation.definitionFit: On the mend is an idiom for recovering from illness, getting better.

clue.text: Sound of engine heading off for space

indicators.note: the head, or first letter, of the word is taken off

parts.note: vroom imitates a revving engine

explanation.surface: A racing car roars away from the start into open space.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heading off' drops the V from VROOM.
explanation.definitionFit: Room in the sense of free space, as in room to move.

clue.text: Class action all over — thrown out

indicators.note: letters all over the place are scattered, signalling a rearrangement
letters thrown about are jumbled into a new order

parts.note: a legal action is a trial
taken as written

explanation.surface: A class-action lawsuit has ended with the case dismissed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Class action' reads as a lawsuit, but 'Class' alone is the definition; 'all over' and 'thrown' jumble TRIAL and OUT.
explanation.definitionFit: A tutorial is a teaching session, a small class with a tutor.

clue.text: Group of soldiers and police have run-in

indicators.note: the first piece is put in the second

parts.note: cops is slang for police
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: Troops and police officers clash in a run-in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'run-in' looks like a quarrel; split it, R (run) goes in COPS.
explanation.definitionFit: A corps is a military unit or body of troops.

clue.text: Allegation in-accordance with information initially received by child

parts.note: as per means in accordance with, as per instructions

indicators.note: the letter goes inside the child, as if taken in by him

parts.note: a son is a child

indicators.note: only the first letter of information is used

explanation.surface: A claim is passed on by a youngster in line with what they were told.
explanation.definitionFit: An aspersion is a damaging charge or slur against someone.

clue.text: Stocking, for instance, book that's put on line

parts.note: Hos. is the standard abbreviation for the Bible book of Hosea
i.e., id est, means that is
RY is the abbreviation for railway, a line

explanation.surface: A stocking or a book is pegged out on the washing line.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'put on' means placed above, so RY comes last.
explanation.definitionFit: Stockings, socks and tights are all items of hosiery.

clue.text: Treat — two I ought to deny myself

indicators.note: to treat material is to process it, so these letters are reworked

explanation.surface: Faced with two treats, I feel I should refuse.
explanation.definitionFit: To go without is to do without something, to deny oneself.

clue.text: Lines learnt by old hands

explanation.surface: Old hands memorise their lines.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lines' suggests an actor's script; experienced people are said to know the ropes.
explanation.definitionFit: Ropes are lines on a ship; old hands know the ropes, the procedures they have learnt.

clue.text: A sin? Yes

parts.note: greed is one of the seven deadly sins

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether something is a sin and gets an affirmative.
explanation.definitionFit: Agreed is an expression of assent, used just like yes.

clue.text: Jam book behind piano

indicators.note: the book comes after the piano

parts.note: P is the musical abbreviation for piano, softly
to book a table is to reserve it

explanation.surface: Jars of jam are kept behind the piano.
explanation.walkthrough: 'book' is the verb, not a volume.
explanation.definitionFit: Preserve is fruit jam or a similar conserve.

clue.text: Wet blanket getting more wet

explanation.surface: A killjoy gets soggier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wet blanket' looks like a soaked blanket, but it means a spoilsport.
explanation.definitionFit: A damper is something that dulls enjoyment; damper is also the comparative of damp.

clue.text: Illicit drink? That's twaddle

explanation.surface: Someone dismisses talk of bootleg liquor as nonsense.
explanation.definitionFit: Moonshine is illegally distilled spirit, and also foolish talk or nonsense.

clue.text: Blame a business centre for avarice

parts.note: to take the rap is to take the blame
the City is London's financial district

explanation.surface: Greed is blamed on a commercial district.
explanation.walkthrough: THE CITY is London's financial district.
explanation.definitionFit: Rapacity is grasping greed, a synonym of avarice.

clue.text: Michael, perhaps, making a move from side to side

parts.note: R is right, one side
a change is a move
L is left, the other side

explanation.surface: Someone called Michael is shuffling sideways.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from side to side' gives the move between two sides: right, R, before and left, L, after.
explanation.definitionFit: Michael is one of the archangels in Christian tradition, so an example.

clue.text: Chap, to you and me, appears avaricious

parts.note: cove is old slang for a chap or fellow
taken as written
us is you and me together

explanation.surface: A fellow strikes the two of us as greedy.
explanation.definitionFit: Covetous means greedily desiring what others have, close to avaricious.

clue.text: Bloomer causing avalanche?

parts.note: a flower read as a fall of snow, a drop that might set off a slide

explanation.surface: A blunder sets off a mountain slide.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bloomer' looks like a mistake but is a flower.
explanation.definitionFit: The snowdrop is a white flower blooming in late winter, so a bloomer.

clue.text: Divine, investing in poor TESSA, is most unhappy

indicators.note: to invest is to clothe or surround, so DD goes into the other letters
poor signals the letters are in poor order, rearranged

parts.note: DD is Doctor of Divinity, a divine

explanation.surface: A clergyman putting money into Tessa's poor account is miserable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Divine' looks like a verb or adjective but is a clergyman, a DD. A TESSA was a British tax-free savings account, which makes 'investing' look financial.
explanation.definitionFit: Saddest is the superlative of sad, meaning most unhappy.

clue.text: Euphoric, in ecstasy, with beautiful views unfolding in turn

indicators.note: the hidden run is turned round and read backwards
the run of letters unfolds from within the words

explanation.surface: Someone euphoric and ecstatic watches lovely vistas open up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unfolding' finds CINECS in 'euphoriC IN ECStasy'; 'in turn' reads it backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Scenic describes a place offering beautiful scenery or views.

clue.text: Happy with what's inside

explanation.surface: Someone is pleased with what is in the box.
explanation.definitionFit: Content means satisfied, and also the material contained in something.

clue.text: "It's a calamity!" I'd assert, furiously

indicators.note: furious action scatters the letters into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone angrily insists that things have gone terribly wrong.
explanation.definitionFit: A disaster is a calamity, a sudden great misfortune.

clue.text: It's comfortably smooth, but vessels capsize

indicators.note: when boats capsize they turn over, so the word is turned round

parts.note: keels is poetic for ships

explanation.surface: Boats overturn even though it all looks smooth.
explanation.definitionFit: Sleek means glossy and smooth, often suggesting a well-fed comfort.

clue.text: A big fish petty officer found in lake

indicators.note: the officer is found inside the lake

parts.note: a tarn is a small mountain lake
PO is the naval abbreviation for petty officer

explanation.surface: A naval officer is discovered in a lake with a large fish.
explanation.definitionFit: The tarpon is a large game fish of warm Atlantic waters.

clue.text: Lamps refurbished as part of service

indicators.note: something refurbished is done up again, so the letters are reworked

explanation.surface: Church lamps are restored as part of a service.
explanation.definitionFit: A psalm is a sacred song sung as part of a church service.

clue.text: Spots madcap

explanation.surface: Someone notices a wild character.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spots' looks like a verb; it is the noun, a skin eruption.
explanation.definitionFit: A rash is an outbreak of spots on the skin, and rash also means reckless, like madcap.

clue.text: Posh type

explanation.surface: An upper-class sort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'type' looks like a kind of person; it is a typewriter typeface.
explanation.definitionFit: Elite means the select upper class; Elite is also a typewriter typeface size.

clue.text: Squash two areas into a' few lines

indicators.note: the areas go into the poem

parts.note: an ode is a short poem, a few lines of verse
a range is an area, as of mountains or grazing land
A is the abbreviation for area

explanation.surface: A sports court is squeezed into a few lines on a plan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Squash' looks like a verb or the sport; it is the British fruit drink made with water.
explanation.definitionFit: Squash is a British fruit cordial, and orangeade is an orange-flavoured drink of that kind.

clue.text: Theme skittishly developed without restriction

indicators.note: a theme developed is worked into a new form, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A composer playfully develops a musical theme with no restraint.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means there is no upper limit, that anything is possible without restriction.
